vs_published_0627.sqrt: +0.005 (0.6 SE) — NOT a defensible SOTA claim

defensible_finding: sqrt weighting beats uniform averaging by +0.020 with sd 0.0089 over 25 seeds — about 2.3 SE. That comparison is internal (same folds, same target, same blocks), so it is a solid result even though the margin over the published number is not.
secondary: A closed-form CKA-learned weighting (0.6195) does WORSE than the hand-chosen sqrt rule, so the simple rule wins.
honest_verdict: Claim: 'resolution-weighted kernel ensembling is a real, reproducible improvement over uniform ensembling.' Do NOT claim: 'we beat the state of the art.'
